newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt sells off 10 pct of MIB.
newsitem.headline: Egypt sells off 10 pct of MIB.

text.p: Egypt's state-owned Banque Misr sold off to the private sector 10 percent of Misr International Bank (MIB) at 310 pounds per share, the flotation agent said on Wednesday.

The offer was ten times oversubscribed, with investors applying for 3.607 million shares worth 1.1 billion pounds, vice president of Concord International Investments, Mohamed el-Ahmady, told Reuters.
Banque Misr owns 55.65 percent of MIB's total 3.75 million shares.
Individual investors got 38.28 percent of the 370,000 on offer. Mutual funds received 35.44 percent, while 26.28 percent went to investment firms, Ahmady said.
Banque Misr has said shareholders will be eligible for an unspecified dividend and a 1/4 bonus share for the 1996 financial year, which ends on December 31.
The state's Misr Insurance owns four percent and Egyptian individuals own 11.35 percent.

Foreign investors include Banca di Roma International (10 percent), British Arab Commercial Bank (8.5 percent), Commerzbank and Central Hispano Americano Banco (jointly 7.875 percent) and Sakura Bank Limited (2.625 percent).
MIB, which has a capital of $37.5 million, has said its net profits rose 60 percent in the first half of calendar year 1996 to 64 million pounds from 40 million pounds for the same period of 1995.
The bank's total assets rose to 9,034 million pounds on June 30, 1996, from 7,823 million one year earlier.
